desc: Implement integer factorization for N up to 1e9 using trial division up to sqrt(N).
Write a deterministic Miller–Rabin primality test for 64-bit integers.

For each test case: handle N=1 as (2,1); otherwise factor N, then search k = 1, 2, 3, … computing p = k·N + 1; for each p that is prime, check pow(2, N, p) == 1 and for every prime divisor q of N check pow(2, N//q, p) != 1; the first p satisfying all conditions is the answer M, with A = 2.
Read T test cases, output "A M" per line.
Include fallback M = 2^N - 1 for N ≤ 60 and try bases 3, 5, 7, 11, 13 if prime search with base 2 fails.
Test the current solution with the provided sample input to confirm output format and correctness; ensure no runtime errors.
Verify edge cases: N=1, N=2, N=3, N=16, N=55, and a large N (e.g., 1e9) to confirm the search terminates and stays within bounds.
If the prime search is too slow for large N, consider precomputing small primes or optimizing the loop; ensure the fallback construction works for all N.
